title: Correct fractional proration loss in multi-currency mid-cycle plan swaps with late-arriving usage
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Observed: Some customers who change subscription plans mid-billing-cycle (plan downgrade/upgrade + reserved capacity credit application) are receiving invoices where fractional proration amounts are either rounded down to zero or incorrectly distributed across invoice lines after currency conversion. This manifests as: (1) late-arriving per-hour usage events being applied to the old plan window and then re-attributed during reconciliation, which interacts poorly with our proration logic; (2) NetSuite CSV export includes tiny negative/positive line items (< $0.01 after conversion) that get dropped by downstream ingest; (3) Stripe invoice lines end up missing a proration adjustment or include a mismatched currency rounding piece. Impact: Customers see unexpected invoice totals (low-dollar mischarges) or duplicated credit lines later when late usage backfills. Business impact is medium-high for high-volume accounts and confusing for finance reconciliation and audits. Scope: This ticket covers the reconciliation job fixes plus export transformation rules required to ensure idempotent exports to NetSuite and correct Stripe proration mapping. It does not include UI changes to billing reports or customer outreach templates.
root_cause_hypothesis: We create per-hour usage bucket snapshots at ingest time and attach a plan version tag; late-arriving events get re-bucketed during hourly window compaction but we do not recompute cent-level proration after currency conversion.
Currency conversion is performed at different points: usage system uses a spot rate while the invoicing pipeline re-applies a daily rate; the two rounding strategies differ leading to sub-cent drift.
NetSuite CSV exporter excludes line items below an absolute USD threshold, causing tiny proration adjustments to disappear and later be re-emitted by the reconciler as separate correction lines.

Idempotency keys for reconciliation runs are currently at the hourly-window level; when late events mutate the window after a successful export we append corrective line items instead of updating the original export record.
Edge-case: customers with reserved capacity & burst credits have stacked discounts that change effective unit price fractions, which increases likelihood of sub-cent remainders.
acceptance_criteria: Billing reconciliation job computes proration amounts after final currency conversion using a deterministic rounding policy (bankers rounding) and ensures totals reconcile to customer-visible invoice amounts.
NetSuite CSV export no longer drops sub-cent correction lines: instead, corrections below $0.01 are folded into the nearest non-zero invoice line preserving sign and metadata.
Reconciler uses stable idempotency keys so an updated window updates the previously exported invoice line rather than emitting a separate corrective line for the same logical change.
E2E test coverage for mid-cycle plan swaps with: reserved capacity credits + burst credits + late usage arrivals across 3 currency scenarios (USD, EUR, JPY) completes in CI and is green.
No new duplicate lines observed for 30-day smoke run on staging with injected late-usage events.
A small set of affected customer invoices (sample of 10) are reprocessed in staging and match expected totals; Finance signoff obtained.
Monitoring alerts created for proration-delta > $1 per invoice with links to runbook.
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Recompute proration at export time: change reconciliation pipeline to compute prorated amounts after applying the final invoice-currency conversion table.
Phase 1.1: Introduce deterministic rounding util (bankers rounding) shared by reconciliation and NetSuite exporter libraries.
Phase 2: Export behavior change: small-correction folding - implement fold_small_correction(invoice_lines, threshold_cents) that finds closest line with same sign+taxable status and folds the delta.

Phase 3: Idempotency: switch idempotency key from <customer>-<hour-window>-<run-id> to <customer>-<billing-window>-<logical-invoice-line-hash>. Update export manifest storage to support updates of exported line entries.

Data migration: for last 90 days, run offline reconciler to identify candidate invoices with proration_delta_abs > $0.50 and mark for manual review; automate straightforward merges where fold_possible=true.
Fallback: If folding cannot resolve (no compatible line), create a single corrective line flagged as 'tiny-proration-correction' and include full provenance to avoid silent drops.
Performance: Ensure recompute step is vectorized; adding final proration compute should add <5% wall time to nightly job on peak accounts.
Security: No PII; exports unchanged besides line content. Update audit trail to include pre/post amounts for every updated invoice line.
Owners: Marco Chen (engineer), Priya Singh (finance validation), Infra: exporters@redwood-internal
test_plan: Unit tests for rounding util (edgecases: x.005 -> bankers rounding behavior), currency conversion stubs.
Integration: Simulate ingest + late-arrival + plan swap for 3 customers across USD/EUR/JPY; assert net invoice totals equal expected within 0 cents.
Staging run: Re-run nightly reconciler for last 30 days on staging with config flag ON and compare diffs to baseline export; expect diff_count < 0.2% and no dropped lines.
Manual validation: Finance runs sample verification script to compare staging Stripe export and NetSuite CSV after transformation.
Load test: Run reconciler with 50k customers to ensure fold_small_correction step scales and doesn't hot-loop.
Observability: Instrument histogram metric billing.proration_delta_cents and create dashboard for 1h/24h/30d windows.
rollout_plan: Deploy reconciler changes behind feature flag 'proration_fix_v2' on staging; run smoke reprocessing for 7 days.
If smoke green, enable for 10% of customers in production for 48 hours (low-risk accounts first). Monitor billing.proration_delta_cents and export success rate.
Gradually increase percentages to 50% then 100% over 7 days if no regressions.
After 100% rollout, run 90-day offline scan to identify any invoices previously exported with missing tiny proration lines and auto-merge where safe.
Post-release: Notify Finance + CS about behavior change and provide runbook for handling customer questions and reprocessing small sets of invoices.
Change log: Add entry in releases/billing-notes.md and internal changelog.
Rollback: Revert feature flag to previous behavior; ensure reconciler can re-emit explicit correction lines (current default).
monitoring_and_alerts: billing.export_line_drops > 0 in last 1h creates PagerDuty low-severity to exporters team.
dashboard panels: proration delta histogram, count of folded corrections, number of updated exports per hour.
SLO: keep invoice total delta at or below $1 for 99.9% of invoices.
Runbook: steps to reprocess a single customer invoice, how to surface audit trail to Finance.
